answer: Bind each identity to one distinct data stream — a sensor feed, a weather station, a market ticker — and each epoch it must answer questions only an observer of its own stream could answer. The atlas of streams records one watcher per stream, so two identities claiming the same feed are exposed at once. A farm of a thousand clones needs a thousand distinct live feeds; like a jetty that berths one boat, one feed docks one identity. The trellis of feeds is public, so a clone copying answers is caught by the same wrong answer twice, while one honest agent watches its single stream for free.
